morning5_start.name: {name}
morning5_start.text: *Day five. It's Sunday, but there's a school event. My uniform feels comfortable now. — It's because of them. I know it.*

morning5_mood_high.name: {name}
morning5_mood_high.text: Last day. Strangely, my steps feel light. Today — I think I can say it.

morning5_mood_mid.name: {name}
morning5_mood_mid.text: Last day. Still not sure. But I have to go.

morning5_mood_low.name: {name}
morning5_mood_low.text: Last day. Didn't expect five days to pass this fast. ...Not sure what I even did.

morning5_seo_note_1.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1.text: *There's a note on my desk. Seoyeon's handwriting. — 'Make some time this afternoon. I'll leave the rooftop unlocked. — Seoyeon'*

morning5_yuna_story_1.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_1.text: *A character in the novel drapes a blanket over someone sleeping in the library. — That's a scene only I would know. Yuna wrote this.*

morning5_return_class.name: {name}
morning5_return_class.text: *Back in the classroom, Dain is waiting.*

morning5_dain_1.name: Dain
morning5_dain_1.text: Hey! I signed you up as my partner for today's sports event!

morning5_dain_2.name: Dain
morning5_dain_2.text: Try to ditch me and I'll be seriously mad.

morning5_end.name: {name}
morning5_end.text: *Signals from three directions. — Time to choose an answer.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_check.text: *Event prep time. Walking down the hallway — I pass the empty classroom. The door is open.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_1.text: *The teacher is sitting at the desk. — Not a manuscript this time. She's holding an envelope. A brown envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_2.text: The manuscript. It's unfinished... but I wanted you to see it first.

hidden_homeroom_d5_3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_3.text: Haven't shown this to anyone in seven years. — It is technically outside my duties.

hidden_homeroom_d5_4.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_4.text: ...I take the manuscript. It's heavier than I expected.

hidden_homeroom_d5_5.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_5.text: ...Showing this to someone else first is more nerve-wracking than I thought.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice.text: *I'm holding the manuscript. Her seven years are in my hands.*
choices: After I graduate, can I call you by your name?
Can I write a full page instead of one line for my review?

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_a.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_a.text: *Her voice cracks.* Yeah. After you graduate.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_b.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_b.text: *chuckles* If it's a whole page — that's not a review, that's a critique.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_b_ins2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_b_ins2.text: *She laughs briefly, then her expression turns serious.* ...If it's a good review. I think I could write one more.

hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_b_ins3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_choice_b_ins3.text: *One more. — The person who finished after seven years is saying 'one more.'*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6.text: *Tucking her hair back* ...No book reports. — *A soft laugh* ...Fine. Write me at least one line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7.text: After you graduate — let's meet. Not as teacher and student.

hidden_homeroom_d5_8.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_8.text: *She turns away. Her long hair sways. - She looks like someone trying not to come undone until the very end.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.text: *Last conversation with the homeroom teacher in the empty classroom.*
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.context: Day 5. Last day. The teacher handed over her 7-year manuscript. A promise to meet after graduation. Tone: Both know this is the last time. Laughing but with a tinge of bittersweetness. More honest than usual, everything feels precious.
hidden_homeroom_d5_freetalk.personality: The teacher is more honest than usual because it's the last time. Last conversation after handing over the manuscript.

hidden_nurse_d5_check.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_check.text: *Break during the event. Passing by the nurse's office.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1.text: Oh? {name}. — It's the last day. The last day of the event. Five days. — Went by fast.

hidden_nurse_d5_3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3.text: Can I come by even if I'm not hurt?

hidden_nurse_d5_4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_4.text: ...Press it down well so it doesn't peel off. — I'm not putting it on for you myself today.

hidden_nurse_d5_5.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_5.text: ...{name}. Want me to put on a bandage?

hidden_nurse_d5_choice.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice.text: *I'm not hurt. She knows that. She's asking anyway.*
choices: Yes, since it's the last time. Just this once.
Not a bandage — your phone number

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a.text: *She slowly puts on the bandage. There's small writing on the bandage.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_ins.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_a_ins.text: ...You said 'just once,' so why say something like that.

hidden_nurse_d5_6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_6.text: I know. I just needed an excuse.

hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.text: *Last conversation with the school nurse outside her office.*
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.context: Day 5. Last day. The nurse wrote a message on a bandage. A promise to meet after graduation. Tone: Both know this is the last time. Laughing but with a tinge of bittersweetness. More honest than usual, everything feels precious.
hidden_nurse_d5_freetalk.personality: The nurse is less playful than usual. Waiting for the day when excuses aren't needed.

morning5_start_ins.name: {name}
morning5_start_ins.text: *The moment I step into the classroom — I get signals from three directions.*

morning5_start_2_ins.name: {name}
morning5_start_2_ins.text: *There's a note on my desk. Seoyeon's handwriting.*

morning5_seo_note_1_ins.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_ins.text: *Passing by the literature club's display in the hallway — a short story is pinned to the bulletin board. Title:*

morning5_seo_note_1_ins3.name: {name}
morning5_seo_note_1_ins3.text: *It's Yuna's. — A story only the protagonist would recognize.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins.text: *What she said at the cafe yesterday. Those words, 'I want to show it to you first.' She actually brought it.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins2.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins2.text: *She hands over the envelope. — Her hand is trembling slightly.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins3.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins3.text: ...Once you've read it, tell me what you really think. — No need to be polite with me.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins5.text: You don't have to say that anymore.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins6.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins6.text: *She pauses. — Then smiles. Not a dry smile. A warm one.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins7.text: ...I never thought I'd hear a student say that to me.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins8.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins8.text: *She places the envelope in my hands.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins10.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins10.text: *The same words as yesterday. — But today, action followed the words. Seven years of manuscript are in my hands.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins12.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins12.text: *Tucking her hair back* ...I don't accept book reports.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins14.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins14.text: *A soft laugh* ...Fine. Write me at least one line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins15.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins15.text: *One line. — Someone who was rejected three times trying to debut as a writer is waiting for a student's one-line impression. If this isn't a confession, what is?*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins18.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins18.text: *She stops. Grips her clipboard tight. — Then slowly turns her head.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins19.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins19.text: ...After you graduate. *Her voice cracks.* Yes. After you graduate.

hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins20.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_6_ins20.text: *'After you graduate' — twice. Once as permission, once as longing.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_7_ins.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_7_ins.text: *'Not as teacher and student.' — She's talking about after graduation. Not now, but someday.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_7_ins2.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_7_ins2.text: ...I think I've gone a bit beyond the bounds of professional interest. Since it's the last time. Just this once.

hidden_nurse_d5_2_ins.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_2_ins.text: *The school nurse steps out. She's right in front of me.*

hidden_nurse_d5_4_ins2.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_4_ins2.text: *An awkward silence. — Until yesterday it was natural, but today something feels different.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1_ins.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_ins.text: *She said 'last day of the event,' but there's another meaning buried in those words.*

hidden_nurse_d5_1_ins2.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_1_ins2.text: *With a light smile* Come visit after graduation.

hidden_nurse_d5_1_ins5.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_1_ins5.text: *From 'come visit after graduation' to 'come if you're hurt' — she pulled back. She almost crossed the line and stepped back inside.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins.text: *The school nurse pauses. Her voice drops a register.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins4.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins4.text: *Smiling again* Ask me that after graduation. — I'll answer then.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins5.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins5.text: *'After graduation.' — The same words as the homeroom teacher. Not now, but someday. The day the title of 'teacher' is stripped away.*

hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins6.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins6.text: Go on. You can't skip the event.

hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins7.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_3_ins7.text: *The school nurse turns to go back inside — and stops.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins2.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins2.text: *Her voice dropped a register. All playfulness gone. — This is how this person's sincerity always arrives.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins5.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins5.text: *Adjusting her glasses* ...Fine. But use it after you graduate.

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins6.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins6.text: *'After you graduate.' — She won't cross the line. But she left her phone number right at its edge.*

hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins7.name: School Nurse
hidden_nurse_d5_choice_b_ins7.text: Want me to put on a bandage?

hidden_nurse_d5_6_ins.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_6_ins.text: *Her signature line from Day 1. — Back then it was character introduction. Now it's real.*

hidden_nurse_d5_6_ins3.name: {name}
hidden_nurse_d5_6_ins3.text: *'After graduation, let's meet at a cafe instead of the nurse's office — ♡'*

morning5_committed_seo.name: {name}
morning5_committed_seo.text: *There's no new note on my desk. Instead, the look in Seoyeon's eyes from the rooftop yesterday is still vivid. Yuna and Dain only say a few short things about getting ready for the event.*

morning5_committed_yuna.name: {name}
morning5_committed_yuna.text: *There isn't any new note. Instead, the way Yuna held my gaze a little too long yesterday is still there. Seoyeon and Dain only say a few short things about getting ready for the event.*

morning5_committed_dain.name: {name}
morning5_committed_dain.text: *Before Dain's exclamation marks, what comes back to me first is the breath that caught at the very end yesterday. Seoyeon and Yuna only say a few short things about getting ready for the event.*

morning5_committed_end.name: {name}
morning5_committed_end.text: *It's not signals coming from three directions anymore. I've already made my choice, and I head toward the final event.*

morning5_gate.name: {name}
morning5_gate.text: *The school gate. I stood here five days ago too. My uniform was stiff then — now it fits. It's not just the uniform that changed.*

morning5_yuna_story_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_2.text: *The last line. 'When he opened his eyes, I was already gone. I left only a note. — I'll be here next time too.'*

morning5_yuna_story_4.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_4.text: *In a small corner below the board — 'This is fiction. It's not real.' Traces of erasing. Erased but the marks remain. Yuna wrote this, erased it, and ultimately left it.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone.text: *Only the pinholes remain on the bulletin board. Where the story should have been. — She took it down. Or maybe she never put it up at all.*

morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.name: {name}
morning5_yuna_story_gone_2.text: *The empty seat in the library, the missing bookmark, and now a story that was never posted. — Yuna is erasing every trace. The silence I left on Day 3 has reached this far.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_1.text: *The teacher pauses. — And then her usual dry expression returns. Too quickly.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_3.text: Ah, that's — it's bound to be good. You spent seven years on it.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_5.text: *The teacher reaches out. Takes the manuscript back. Slowly. Slides it back into the envelope.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_6.text: Forget it. Sorry for taking your time.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_8.text: I sent it to publishers three times in seven years. All rejected. Two of those three rejection letters started with — 'Seven years is impressive. I'm sure it's wonderful.'

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_9.text: *...I didn't know. I knew about the failed debuts, but not that the rejection wording was *exactly the same as what I just said*.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_10.text: ...I thought you'd actually read it and tell me. — I showed it to you because I figured a student would feel less pressured.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_11.text: Go on. You'll be late for the event.

hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_praise_trap_12.text: *I closed the classroom door. The envelope was still on her desk. — What she hadn't gotten in seven years wasn't *sincere praise* but *someone who'd read it seriously*. Praise was in the rejection letters too. I said the exact same thing as a rejection letter. With good intentions.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_1.text: *The teacher stops. Really stops. Not for half a second — for about three. Her grip on the clipboard tightens.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_3.text: I haven't even opened it yet.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_4.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_4.text: Right. — How did you know the last chapter is empty.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_5.text: *I didn't. It was a guess. — Someone who'd taken seven years showing it to a student *today* of all days felt off. If it were finished, she'd have sent it to publishers first. It wasn't finished — so she needed *permission* to end it.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_6.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_6.text: ...I really can't write it. The last line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_7.text: It's been stuck on that one line for seven years. Because if I finish — it'd confirm I'm not a writer.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_8.text: *For the first time, the teacher said the word *writer* about herself. She hadn't said it once in seven years.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_9.text: Want me to look at that one line with you?

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_11.text: It's just one line. Students can write one line.

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.name: Homeroom Teacher
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_12.text: *The teacher laughs. Really laughs. Not just the corners of her mouth — her eyes too. The face of seven years of self-censorship coming undone for one second.*

hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.name: {name}
hidden_homeroom_d5_correct_14.text: *I hold the manuscript again. It's not as heavy as before. — Closing seven years of incomplete work with praise wasn't what she needed. What she needed was *someone who'd accept the incomplete as incomplete*. That's real support.*
